transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-02
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Thompson (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Nexa Eng Mgr), Maya Singh (Nexa SRE), Samir Patel (Nexa DS), Leah Ortiz (Nexa Security)

[00:00] Alex Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call, we got Jordan, Maya, Samir, Leah, yep?
[00:05] Jordan Lee: Yep here, thanks Alex.
[00:08] Maya Singh: Hi all.
[00:10] Priya Kapoor: Hi folks, Priya from Redwood.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Samir here.
[00:15] Leah Ortiz: Leah here.

[00:20] Alex Thompson: Cool, agenda for today, quick onboarding status, confirm access + VPC peering, plan the latency benchmark, go through any security questions, and then next steps. Anything you want to add?
[00:30] Jordan Lee: No that looks right. We're mainly focused on getting the private env talking to your dedicated pool, and then running the baseline tests.

[00:45] Priya Kapoor: Great, quick status from our side: we saw the service account created yesterday, we have API keys provisioned for the test cluster, but we still need the VPC peering details and egress IPs from your side to whitelist. We also prepared a short inference tuning guide - sent a link in the chat - that shows batch/quantization settings we typically use.
[01:05] Maya Singh: Yeah, so on our side we created the peering request but our network team needs to confirm routes. Also firewall blocks all outbound non-whitelisted IPs so we need the specific egress range.
[01:18] Alex Thompson: Understood, Maya. We'll share the egress ranges and ephemeral IP ranges for the dedicated cluster. Note those can vary slightly between regions but we'll call out the primary ones.

[01:32] Samir Patel: Quick question on data handling - when we send requests in the POC, does Redwood persist logs? We need to know for the privacy review.
[01:40] Alex Thompson: Good question. For Hosted API we retain transient logs for X days, for Dedicated/Private when it's a dedicated pool data retention options are configurable and we can disable retention per your contract; I'll include the exact policy in the security packet.
[01:56] Leah Ortiz: Please include KMS integration details and audit-log retention. We need to feed into our compliance team.
[02:05] Priya Kapoor: Noted, Leah. We'll attach the SOC2 summary, KMS integration guide, and an example audit log snippet.

[02:18] Jordan Lee: On the benchmarking plan: we want to validate 99th percentile latency under our expected traffic pattern. Samir will run the evals and provide the prompt set. Priya, what's the recommended load pattern to replicate production?
[02:32] Priya Kapoor: For discovery proofs we typically do a ramp to 50 concurrent sessions with bursts to 100, using sequence lengths of 128 and 512 tokens to cover both short and long cases. We'll provide the harness script (k6 or locust examples) and parameters.
[02:49] Samir Patel: We'll also evaluate embedding throughput for search indexing use case; that's separate but we can run it same week.

[03:00] Maya Singh: I want to flag that our egress rules also require a curl-based healthcheck from our side before we can open peering fully. We can do that once you provide the IP allowlist.
[03:12] Alex Thompson: That's fine - we'll add a short checklist for the network handoff.

[03:25] Jordan Lee: Any concerns about cost? Our finance lead asked about dedicated minimums vs hosted run cost for the POC.
[03:34] Alex Thompson: For short pilots hosted is often cheaper since there is no commit, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token unit cost. I'll send a comparison table in the follow-up.
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: And technically, for the benchmarks if you want the lowest latency path we can run a dedicated pool in the same region to minimize cross-region hops. Also quantization profiles can shave 15-30% cost with small latency tradeoffs.
[04:00] Jordan Lee: Cool. Also vendor question - our procurement asked if you have any customers using Anthropic or OpenAI side-by-side; just for understanding compatibility.
[04:10] Alex Thompson: We have customers who mix providers; we can support fallback routing policies and highlight where models differ in behaviour. We'll include notes on model parity.

[04:25] Leah Ortiz: Anything on SSO? We want to ensure account access maps to our IdP (SAML).
[04:30] Alex Thompson: Yes - Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can centralize auth to your IdP. We'll include the SSO setup doc in the pack.

[04:42] Priya Kapoor: Quick demo note - last week we left on a failed inference due to missing KV cache warmup; we pushed a small script to the repo that preloads cache. Jordan, did you try it?
[04:54] Jordan Lee: Samir did, we saw improvements for repeated context but still saw 5-10% variability.
[05:00] Priya Kapoor: Ok great, we'll tune the warmup script and send a revised version.

[05:10] Alex Thompson: Let's make sure timeline is clear: network + security docs this week, benchmark run next week, and then decision framework (Hosted vs Dedicated) after results. Any blockers?
[05:22] Maya Singh: Network team is the blocker; they'll only approve once they see egress ranges and the brief healthcheck steps.
[05:30] Leah Ortiz: Security wants the SOC2 and KMS details - procurement will hold otherwise.

[05:40] Alex Thompson: Action items recap then: Priya will run benchmarks and share script; Maya to confirm network and send screenshot; Alex to share security pack and pricing; Samir to share prompt sets.
[05:52] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Can we capture the specific dates?
[05:55] Alex Thompson: Yes - we'll aim to have the security pack and pricing by Thursday 2027-06-03, Maya's screenshot by Friday 2027-06-04, Samir's prompts by Monday 2027-06-07, and the benchmark results in time for the 2027-06-09 run.

[06:16] Priya Kapoor: One more technical note - for the embedding throughput test please ensure batch sizes reflect your indexing pipeline; default bench is batch 64 but if you use micro batches tell us.
[06:28] Samir Patel: We'll verify, probably batch 32 for our pipeline.

[06:36] Alex Thompson: Great. Anything else from the team?
[06:40] Maya Singh: One ask: can Redwood provide sample firewall rules for AWS TGW peering? That would speed our network review.
[06:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes - we'll attach AWS TGW example rules and a GCP snippet if needed.

[06:56] Leah Ortiz: Also please include a redaction/PII policy for logs.
[07:00] Alex Thompson: Will do.

[07:05] Alex Thompson: Alright, thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the pack and I'll set the benchmark schedule invite for 2027-06-09 10:00 PT.
[07:12] Jordan Lee: Thanks all.
[07:14] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings - e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cache, TGW as T G W, and minor filler words preserved.
